Wes Moore

Democratic candidate for Governor / Lt. Governor, Maryland · Incumbent

Governor of Maryland (incumbent)

Wes Moore is the 63rd governor of Maryland. He was first elected in 2022, when he defeated Republican Dan Cox, and took office on January 18, 2023. He won the Democratic primary on June 23, 2026, and is running for reelection with Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller.

Where Moore stands

Affordability / cost of living
Says he will drive down costs by creating jobs, building more affordable housing and introducing legislation against price gouging.
Energy / utility bills
Proposes lowering energy bills by having Maryland produce more of its own energy. Says the state should reverse its position as a net energy importer.
Data centers
Says his approach to data centers has changed because their growth and energy demand have changed. In the Oct. 6 debate he pointed to a recent executive order and did not back a moratorium on new data centers.
Immigration enforcement
Opposes letting ICE agents deputize state and local police. Says the state will keep working with federal partners to hold violent offenders accountable.
Economy and jobs
Says Maryland added nearly 100,000 jobs and more than 35,000 new businesses in three years. Pledges more legislation and action to keep job growth going.
Health care
Says he has fought to fund rural hospitals and to make quality health care accessible across the state, regardless of zip code.
Elections / voting
Points to laws passed to protect election workers. Says he will keep Maryland's elections free and fair.
Redistricting (Ballot Question 3)
Supports Question 3, a constitutional amendment that would loosen standards for congressional redistricting. Says he will vote yes on it.

Background

  • Governor of Maryland, 2023–present
  • Chair, National Governors Association, 2026–present
  • U.S. Army and Army Reserve officer, 1998–2014 (captain, 82nd Airborne Division; served in Afghanistan; Bronze Star)
  • A.A., Valley Forge Military College
  • B.A., Johns Hopkins University
  • M.Litt., Wolfson College, Oxford
